abstract: A novel method to change the bit-rate of MPEG-2 video streams is proposed. It is based on an adaptive quantizer and single-pass variable rate controller. It achieves better quality, without being affected by drift degradation. A software low power implementation is proposed on a powerful SLIW DSP//spl mu/P.

articleTitle: From DCT-based to wavelet-based video transcoding algorithm and architecture design
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: The main advantage of using DWT is to cope with high compression demand and still get good image quality. Nevertheless, most of the image data are discrete-time cosine-transform (DCT) based. For this reason, we propose a DCT-based to DWT-based image transcoder to convert the pre-existent image data. In our paper, we. investigate the inverse discrete-time cosine-transform (IDCT) and DWT mathematical equation in matrix form. In this way, we develop some method to speed up the computation and lower the architecture complexity. We use MATLAB to justify our theoretic study. After software simulation, we use VHDL code and Synopsys to realize our hardware architecture.

articleTitle: HDD characterisation for A/V streaming applications
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: This paper presents a model-based method for the characterization of the real-time streaming performance of hard disc drives (HDD) and shows how to extract the model parameters automatically from service time measurements of only standard read and write commands.

articleTitle: Software optimization of the MPEG-audio decoder using a 32-bit MCU RISC processor
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: This paper proposes optimization techniques to implement MPEG audio decoding algorithms in real-time using a general-purpose 32-bit MCU RISC processor. We implemented an MP3/AAC decoder using an ARM-based RISC MPU and its test board. Both the designed decoders with the proposed optimizations could achieve decoding processes in real-time within an operating frequency of 35 MHz.

articleTitle: Development of a new consumer VCR format and high density magnetic recording using MR head
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: This paper presents a new consumer VCR format, MICROMV, and a high density recording system which uses the MR (magneto resistive) head. A small-sized cassette of 12 cc volume stores one-hour of 12 Mbit/s MPEG2 picture, which corresponds to 6.5 gigabytes of data. The MR head system realizes the areal density of 0.8 Gbit/inch/sup 2/ which is more than 3 times as large as that of the DVC format.

articleTitle: MNR: a novel approach for temporal filtering of MPEG distortions
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: As TV screens get ever larger, viewer tolerance to noise and artefacts has steadily declined. For next generation TVs such as flat TV, LCoS (liquid crystal on silicon), etc, being excellent in picture quality becomes a distinguishing feature. Although the quality of most digital signals has significantly been improved, distortion and noise still creep in and are an important source of picture degradations. Post-processing is a sensible solution that achieves a visual enhancement of the reconstructed images. Some of the artefacts, such as blocking and ringing, have already been widely considered. Therefore, this paper concentrates on a novel post-processing technique, that reduces another kind of distortion known as "mosquito noise". This temporal "busyness" is discarded by applying an adaptive temporal filter that preserves sharpness and naturalness of the reconstructed video signal in the frequency domain. The proposed algorithm is effective and straightforward to implement: experimental results show that the presented temporal post-filtering process significantly improves the visual quality of video. Moreover, the architectural options allow flexibility and cost trade-off.

articleTitle: A reconfigurable audio power amplifier delivering 150 W to 1-/spl Omega/ loudspeakers for in-car sound systems
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: A reconfigurable audio amplifier is proposed. It can be configured to operate as standard dual-bridge, as high-efficiency dual-bridge, or as high-power mono-bridge amplifier. The built-in diagnostic with an I/sup 2/C-bus interface completes the above features. The device delivers to 1/spl Omega/ up to 150W in high-power mode and saves 50% of the dissipated power in high-efficiency configuration.

articleTitle: Enhanced VSB system
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: The authors' companies independently developed enhancements to the existing ATSC (Advanced Television Systems Committee) VSB (vestigial sideband) digital television standard (A/53). Each company's private tests showed its system to be backward compatible with existing ATSC receivers and to offer improvements in flexibility and signal robustness to meet broadcasters' needs. When both systems were submitted to the ATSC committee on enhancements, the two companies found their proposals to be very complementary, resulting in the formation of a joint proposal for enhancement of the VSB digital TV broadcasting system. The combined proposal is described along with its technical benefits. Transmission and receiving hardware for the combined system exists and was tested by the VSB Enhancement Testing Consortium (VETC), an industry group led by MSTV and NAB.

articleTitle: The software headend architecture - a new approach for multi-standard CATV headends
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: Cable television (CATV) networks are in transition to digital two-way broadband networks. The industry has already developed devices according to the Data Over Cable Service Interface Specifications (DOCSIS) or digital video broadcasting (DVB) standards for cable. Both standards are incompatible. This digest introduces a new concept for headends in CATV networks. The goal of the software headend architecture is to handle multiple standards on the same hardware platform. Architectures with flexible signal processing elements are presented and classified. Advantages of this new concept are an easy exchange of standards by setting the appropriate configuration without changing hardware and the possibility to install software headends and software terminals in any cable environment.

articleTitle: 30 GB/side rewritable optical disk for HDTV utilizing a blue laser diode
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: This paper presents a rewritable optical disk with a capacity of 30 GB/side intended for the next generation of rewritable optical disks. The experimental results have shown that this optical disk has wide tilt margin and is a prospective candidate for supplanting VCR in the HDTV era.

articleTitle: A mobile storage device with the magneto-optical disk of a 50 mm diameter and 730 MB capacity
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: A small re-writable optical disk has been proposed. The media, which is called "iD PHOTO" disk, has a diameter of 50 mm and 730 MB capacity. We developed a new storage device with the iD PHOTO disk. In this paper we describe this storage device and the techniques used to realize the iD PHOTO system.

articleTitle: Object based refinement of motion vector fields applying probabilistic homogenization rules
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: This paper presents a new image analysis method, combining motion estimation and image segmentation. Whereas none of these methods, used on its own, delivers error free meta-information an appropriate combination leads to an orthogonalization of these errors. This method is applied to improve the quality of motion vector fields.

articleTitle: DOCSIS/spl trade/ 2.0 - the next revolution in cable modem technology
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: This paper provides an overview of DOCSIS 2.0, the main objective of which is to achieve a significant increase in upstream bandwidth, while providing more robustness against channel impairments. This has been achieved through inclusion of an enhanced physical layer that supports higher order modulations with increased forward error correction capabilities.

articleTitle: The high-quality audio broadcasting system using MPEG-2 AAC and streaming technology
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: This paper describes the implementation of an Internet audio service using MPEG-2 AAC and streaming technology. This system consists of MPEG-2 AAC hardware encoder, the streaming server, the message server, and the client. For the test of the system performance, we are temporally servicing the system in our Institute's intranet environment, which has about 2000 users.

articleTitle: Comparison of two guided scrambling schemes for optical disks
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: Guided scrambling (GS) is a candidate for a DC-free code in the next generation of the DVD standard. This paper evaluates the performance of convolutional GS and GF-addition GS on DC-component suppression and symbol error probability.

articleTitle: A high performance lattice architecture of 2D discrete wavelet transform for hierarchical image compression
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: This paper presents a high performance lattice architecture of 2D discrete wavelet transform (DWT), which is scalable to extend to an arbitrary 2D DWT with M taps and J levels. The proposed lattice structure fits in a VLSI implementation due to its regularity and shows the period of N/sup 2//2 to compute an N/spl times/N image because the even and odd rows are processed simultaneously.

articleTitle: Integrated system for multimedia delivery over broadband IP networks
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: In this paper we describe an integrated system for delivering multimedia content to consumer terminals over broadband IP networks. The system will be the basic component of a future networked consumer electronics content delivery mechanism extending the current TV.

articleTitle: Improvement of low gray scale linearity using multi-luminance-level subfield method in plasma display panel
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: A new multi-luminance-level subfield method is proposed to improve the low gray-level color reproducibility of a plasma display panel. Multi-luminance levels can be expressed per sustain pulse in low gray scale by applying the different auxiliary pulses in the same sustain-pulse subfields, thereby suppressing the low gray-level contour.

articleTitle: Efficient and reliable video transmission with error localization
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: The convergence of Internet, multimedia and mobile applications has led to an increasing demand for efficient and reliable video data transmission over heterogeneous networks. Due to their coding efficiency, variable-length codes (VLC) are usually employed in the entropy coding stage of video compression standards. However, error propagation is a major problem associated with VLC. We propose the use of self-synchronizing VLC (SSVLC) to achieve the dual goal of optimal coding efficiency and optimal error localization. Performance evaluation has revealed that the use of SSVLC provides better performance than standard VLC techniques.

articleTitle: NAMBA: location-aware collaboration system for shopping and meeting
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: This paper proposes new services that exchange location information and the participants' present situation to one another We have developed a location-aware collaboration system called NAMBA that supports the proposed services using PDA with built-in PHS and GPS in real time. We found that location information and chats were important for communication with separated participants. NAMBA was effective for meeting at any places.

articleTitle: Implementation of the turbo-TCM and space-time code modulation with FPGA in transceiver
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: The presence of turbo-TCM and space-time code modulation constitutes a major channel coding in a transceiver. We have designed and simulated a CODEC by Altera in software, which can be improved by FPGA. We also use turbo coding to increase bandwidth efficiency and BAHL and Viterbi decoding to enhance performance. In this paper, the turbo-TCM and space-time code modulation concatenation can improve decoding speed and enhance coding gain relatively without increasing bandwidth in the wireless communication system. We get very good performance from target FPGA with two receive antennas that can increase power gain with an 8 state 8-PSK for the concatenation of TTCM and STBC.

articleTitle: A study on secure wireless networks consisting of home appliances
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: We propose a way of managing wireless home network security which allows appliances to determine whether other appliances belong to the same network. We assume that a way of protecting communication is already provided in the data link layer, and provide a way of distributing an encryption key.

articleTitle: New driving scheme for white color balancing of plasma display panel television
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: A new driving-scheme is used for balancing white colors of plasma display panel-television (PDP-TV) by independent luminance control of the red, green and blue colors. White colors of eight subfields can be clustered within a region, which is not resolvable in terms of visual perception.

articleTitle: An FPGA implementation of a flexible architecture for H.263 video coding
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: In this paper the implementation of an H.263 base-line video coder on an FPGA-based platform is explained. The coder consists of a set of specialised processors for the main tasks (DCT, quantizations, motion estimation) and a RISC for the scheduling tasks. The design has been written in synthesizable Verilog and fully tested with hardware-software co-simulation using standard video sequences. Finally, the coder has been tested on a prototyping board with a RISC processor and an FPGA.

articleTitle: Optimization of queueing performance and embedded I/O buffers for MPEG codec design
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: This paper presents a generalized queueing model and an algorithm to obtain the best performance with the optimized embedded buffers in MPEG-2 codec designs. A generalized queueing model is proposed to apply not only to the MPEG-2 codec system, but also to other MPEG applications, like HDTV and MPEG-4. The searching algorithm is developed to find the optimal solution efficiently by exploring the correlation between buffers and system performance. The local optimum is guaranteed.

articleTitle: Versatile COFDM modulator/demodulator design based on the CORDIC-algorithm
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: This paper discusses the advantages of the CORDIC-algorithm in butterfly-operations (FFT) and numerical controlled oscillator (NCO) which are used in many digital transmission systems. The implementation in programmable logic devices is shown by the example of a versatile demodulator for digital terrestrial television.

articleTitle: New communication style using television broadcasting and the Internet
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: This paper presents (i) a new communication style in which a subject of interest such as a visual object rendered by TV broadcasting is directly linked with chat messages, (ii) a method of grouping TV viewers who are interested in the same visual object, and (iii) a method of sharing thumbnail images without transmitting the video data itself.

articleTitle: Blind decision feedback equalization for VSB-based DTV receivers
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: We present a novel blind decision feedback equalization algorithm for VSB-based DTV receivers by modifying a stop-and-go dual-mode algorithm to improve the performance of convergence speed and residual MSE. Considering VSB modulation and RF-band effects with the baseband-equivalent VSB channel model raises the reliability of our results for practical applications.

articleTitle: Scenario driven evaluation and interference mitigation proposals for Bluetooth and high data rate Bluetooth enabled consumer electronic devices
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: This paper investigates the effects of interference occurring between Bluetooth and high data rate Bluetooth enabled consumer electronic devices in the home and office environment. Software simulated results for frequency collisions between piconets operating in both synchronous and asynchronous modes with typical up and downlink loading factors are presented (for time-bounded and non-time bounded electronic devices). The significance of this interference on the data throughput in a number of example scenarios is investigated using a state-of-the-art indoor space-time propagation model. These results are then compared with measured channel data taken in the test environment using a MEDAV RUSK BRI channel sounder. The paper concludes by proposing to mitigate the effects of interference by employing synchronous communication in future Bluetooth and Bluetooth evolution networks.

articleTitle: SVCDPlus - an extension of SVCD standard
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: SVCDPlus (Super Video Compact Disc Plus) is a new disc standard we developed in China for long playing mode requirements of discs from the Chinese market with a middle level of resolution. We use DVD-ROM as the carrier instead of CD-ROM and still keep the SVCD system format on top such that the playing time can be extended to 4 to 7 hours depending on the average bit rate. This standard fills the gaps between the Chinese market requirement and current available disc standards. We developed the SVCDPlus authoring tools and the SVCDPlus player based on Philips TriMedia board.

articleTitle: Home networking digital TV based on LnCP
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: This paper presents the home networking protocol, LnCP which has been developed to connect home appliances. Then a digital TV that can communicate with other appliances using LnCP is introduced.

articleTitle: Hash function and turbo code for invisible communication
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: This paper presents a blind data hiding technique in still images. The cover image is de-correlated by using the key. The error control channel coding is introduced into the data hiding scheme. The message encrypted is encoded with a turbo coder. The one-way hash function is used in the embedding process. The algorithm for hiding bit selection is proposed and an experimental implementation of the algorithm is presented.

articleTitle: TrueTime software architecture
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: General purpose operating systems do not provide a quality of service (QoS) guarantee for processing isochronous A/V data streams. The TrueTime software architecture provides a model for guaranteed processing of isochronous streams. The TrueTime architecture integrates with an OS kernel to exploit the streaming nature of isochronous data streams.

articleTitle: Adaptive frame selection algorithm for DVB-T
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: A proposed frame selection algorithm is able to remove intersymbol interference (ISI) produced by multipaths in conventional orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) systems. Four estimation methods are also proposed to adaptively determine a replaced period of the proposed algorithm according to multipath conditions.

articleTitle: Development of PDA with global navigation capability
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: This paper presents one of the handheld mobile device paradigms recently developed in the III ESL Laboratory. The device combines personal information tools and global navigation capability based on a private embedded OS running on the ARM platform. Both the software and hardware design considerations are described.

articleTitle: Industry efforts to standardize the car bus
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: The ever increasing complexity of automotive entertainment and information systems has necessitated a universal communication network for vehicles. Intelligent transportation systems (ITS) initiatives have focused on road and rail infrastructure, to enable telematics communications between roadway/railway, vehicles and public agencies, primarily to provide enhanced public services, such as traffic management and emergency response. While the development of infrastructure standards has been largely backed by national governments, standards for an in-vehicle bus platform to support both these enhanced services and the connectivity of consumer electronics (CE) devices have been left to the commercial market to develop. This paper discusses the standardization activities for such a network.

articleTitle: Adaptive QoS control for video transmission over band-limited networks
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: Consumers increasingly demand high quality of service (QoS) for multimedia applications. Application-layer QoS control mechanisms that do not make specific references to coding semantics tend to provide the most robust solutions for delivery of multimedia data over bandlimited networks. We propose an adaptive and robust QoS algorithm for bandlimited networks that integrates explicit receiver-sender rate control, rate shaping with multiple quantization parameters and adaptive FEC.

articleTitle: A multi-agent architecture for intelligent home network service by MASSIHN
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: The major design challenge to realize intelligent home network services is organizing distributed as well as heterogeneous home devices effectively. To meet the design challenge, a mobile agent space based multi-agent architecture is considered in this paper. MASSIHN is a home network system that links consumer electronics and computing devices in the home. The proposed approach can execute MASSIHN applications from many commonly used devices such as PDA and laptops.

articleTitle: Improved region-of-interest image coder and its application
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: In this paper we incorporate multiple ROI coding and data embedded functionalities into the SPIHT codec with the reversible two-ten integer wavelet transform, and propose two improvement schemes of the SPIHT algorithm and utilize a context-based adaptive arithmetic coder to further enhance coding efficiency. Each ROI has individual ellipse or rectangle shape model and possesses its own priority (reconstruction speed). The priority decides the order of processing for the coefficients at encoder and decoder In addition, we propose a method called Odd and Even Number Attachment (OENA) to embed data. The data can be a meaningful image or useful text for some special applications such as digital cameras and digital libraries. We implement a remote monitor system to integrate all techniques. In this system, the luminance is compressed by an improved SPIHT codec, and the chrominance is embedded into the bitstream by OENA. The guarder can decide to use ROI or not, and the bit-rates to transmit to network.

articleTitle: A new concept of multi-functioned mobile phone with virtual display
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: This paper proposes a new concept of mobile telephone with a PC resolution virtual display that has the following five functions: telephone, E-mail, Web telephone, videophone and VOD (video on demand) viewer. We developed a concept proof prototype based on this concept.

articleTitle: Signal circulation for adaptive equalization in digital communication systems
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new approach combining conventional adaptive equalizers with signal circulation for channel equalization enhancement in digital communication systems. With signal circulation functionalities, we may improve the performance of adaptive equalizers, especially when short training sequences are used.

articleTitle: Content-dependent optimization of JPEG2000 compressed images
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: This paper presents a method to optimize the visual quality of JPEG2000-compressed images using an adaptive approach to assign more bits to regions in which errors are more visible, maintaining the global bit-rate unchanged.

articleTitle: HD image retrieval utilizing networked image directory
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: Proposed is an improved multimedia database system, characterized by dedicated design of its user terminal and image directory, featuring the use of HDTV display for faithfully demonstrating the color of Japanese traditional Kosode garments.

articleTitle: Speech synthesis method with a harmonic plus noise model
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: The requirements of text-to-speech synthesis are increasing, since the speech interface is an appropriate user-friendly interface for consumer applications. However, in general, the quality of synthetic speech is not satisfactory, and speech synthesis requires a large amount of computation and memory. In this paper, we propose a high quality speech synthesis method for text-to-speech systems and report its implementation using a FPGA. The experimental results show the proposal method can generate high quality synthetic speech, and we can realize a low-power FPGA-based hardware for consumer applications.

articleTitle: A new readout circuit for an ultra high sensitivity CMOS image sensor
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: We have developed a new readout circuit for highly sensitive CMOS image sensors. The circuit makes it possible to obtain high signal-to-noise ratio (S/N) by effectively transferring signal charges accumulated in the photo-diode (PD) to a smaller capacitance. We fabricated and tested a CMOS image sensor with the readout circuit, and confirmed that it has higher sensitivity than conventional passive-type CMOS image sensors.

articleTitle: High quality image processing for digital still camera
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: We developed three new technologies of color reappearance, resolution and dynamic range for a high quality image. We improved the digital still camera using the developed new technology.

articleTitle: MAC LSI design for wireless MPEG-2 transmission over IEEE802.11b PHY
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: This paper describes a new approach to a hybrid ARQ based MAC protocol scheme to be integrated in a MAC (medium access control) LSI, which is devised for a dedicated wireless AV transmission system over the IEEE802.11b physical layer (PHY). This system is now commercially available with the name of "Smartlink".

articleTitle: A fast audio bit allocation technique based on a linear R-D model
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: This paper describes a fast bit allocation technique using a novel linear model for the bit rate and the global gain of the inner loop in the classic MP3 bit allocation. The outer loop is approximated with a binomial expansion. Our technique is five times faster than the LAME MP3 encoder.

articleTitle: Compressed domain spatial scaling of MPEG video sequences
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: As more and more multimedia content is delivered and stored in the MPEG compressed format, there is an increasing need for compressed domain manipulation techniques. We introduce an efficient method to perform spatial domain scaling of MPEG video. Simulation results indicate that the proposed scheme is faster than the current compressed domain processes while having a comparable subjective quality.

articleTitle: Real-time MPEG video encoder with embedded scene change detection and telecine inverse
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: This paper describes very cost-effective algorithms to detect scene changes and field repetition in video sequences for a real-time MPEG encoder. It also provides a scheme to support a dynamic GOP structure reflecting the detection outcome on the fly. With these features, the encoder can encode video more efficiently in either quality or bitrate aspect. The proposed detection methods only utilize the existing information, field motion vectors and picture coding type, from MPEG coding and are very suitable for (but not limited to) software-based encoders.

articleTitle: Video format conversion in a single chip
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: This paper presents a SoC solution that will provide video format conversion for television sets and DVD players, which provides the highest quality image. The chip accepts and provides various video formats and employs motion adaptive de-interlacing, image conversion and enhancement.

articleTitle: Class-D amplification combined with switched-mode power conditioning - the route to long battery life
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: Class-D amplification is the acknowledged means by which amplifier power demand can be reduced in battery-powered audio products. However, it is also well known that the switching action of the class-D amplifier is a potential source of electromagnetic interference and therefore designers of audio consumer products are naturally concerned that the adoption of this form of amplification will jeopardise the ability of their product to comply with EMC regulations. We show that when properly screened class-D amplifiers can be used within a few inches of a sensitive AM broadcast receiver. Furthermore, the cost of the screening can be defrayed by including switched-mode power management circuits within the screened environment. This reduces power consumption, allows the use of a single cell as power source, and reduces the total ownership cost and the size and weight of the product.

articleTitle: DC-free multimode code design using novel selection criteria for optical recording systems
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: This paper proposes new criteria MPRDS (Minimum Peak Running Digital Sum with Sign Change) and ABSRDS (Absolute Running Digital Sum) schemes for evaluating the quality of candidate codewords in multimode codes. The schemes have similar performance and much simpler complexity compared to MSW (Minimum Squared Weight), which is known to be the best. In addition, this paper also introduces MTO/SC (Minimum Threshold Overrun with Sign Change) and MRDS/SC (Minimum Running Digital Sum with Sign Change) criteria. The MTO/SC and MRDS/SC are the improved versions of conventional MTO and RDS, respectively.

articleTitle: A novel model for spatio-temporally consistent video enhancement
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: Inconsistencies in video enhancement can result in annoying flickering artifacts that are even worse than without enhancement. A model needs to be in place that enforces spatial and temporal consistency as an integral part of the video enhancement.

articleTitle: Efficient video coding integrating MPEG-2 and picture-rate conversion
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: We present an MPEG-2 compatible video codec that uses picture-rate up-conversion during decoding. The up-conversion autonomously regenerates major parts of frames without vectorial or residual data. Consequently, the bit rate is greatly reduced.

articleTitle: Flexible frame-reordering and multi-temporal motion estimation for scalable MPEG encoding in mobile consumer equipment
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: We present a new scalable three-stage motion estimation technique that allows scaling of the computational effort and memory bandwidth usage by a factor of 14. At full processing, our technique slightly outperforms a 128 /spl times/ 128 full search motion estimation.

articleTitle: Automatic measurements of digital receivers using sampled signals
publicationTitle: 2002 Digest of Technical Papers. International Conference on Consumer Electronics (IEEE Cat. No.02CH37300)
abstract: In the present paper we present some considerations to be taken in to account for automatic measurements of consumer electronic front-ends. We use for this approach sampled signals instead of analogue signals. The sampled signals are processed in time and frequency domain using digital signal processing, allowing faster and more effective measurement methods. Measurements of analogue (noise figure, phase noise, IP3) and digital parameters (BER) are explained here on a satellite front-end for digital TV reception.
